jobs.description:
Nofence is a Norwegian scale-up that has built the world’s first virtual fencing solution for livestock. As we aim to revolutionize livestock management, we will need top-notch competence in our Engineering team, and we are now looking for an Industrial Designer.

Your main responsibilities will be:
• 
Generate and visualize design concepts and mechanical solutions for our future livestock hardware products, taking them from early ideas to production-ready models.

• 
Design for manufacturing by cooperation with mechanical and manufacturing engineers.

• 
Develop the design guidelines for industrial design in the company.

• 
Contribute to field research on farms and ranches to observe livestock interactions, working conditions, and operator workflows to inform design concepts.

• 
Design products that prioritize animal welfare, prevent injury, and ensure ergonomic, intuitive handling for farmers and agricultural technicians.

• 
Partner with Product Management and UX design to translate user feedback, field research, and competitive insights into compelling, feasible physical product concepts.

We are looking for someone who has:
• 
Bachelor or Master degree in industrial or product design.

• 
Experience designing electro-mechanical products for volume manufacturing.

• 
Excellent visualization skills on paper and with physical and digital models.

• 
Creative problem-solving skills for complex design solutions.

We are looking for someone who is:
• 
Motivated by working in an autonomous cross-functional team.

• 
Structured with the ability to bridge the gap between user needs and design for manufacturing.

• 
Motivated to facilitate workshops and creative sessions.

• 
Comfortable working in an English-speaking work environment.

• 
Drivers license and ability to travel abroad.

About Nofence
Managing livestock has always been a challenge. Humanity has tried everything from herding with dogs to walling the animals in with barbed wire, electric, and wooden fences, but these are costly and time-consuming solutions and often in conflict with the local wildlife. It has also left vast areas of potential pasture overgrown and underutilized.

Until now.
Enter virtual fences. What started as a small group of farmers and engineers with a big idea has become Nofence – the world’s first virtual fencing solution for livestock.

What we bring to the table
At Nofence, we're not your typical 9-to-5 gig. We're a dynamic scale-up, creating a work atmosphere that's anything but ordinary. It's a place where dedication and innovation are the norm, offering great opportunities for your personal and professional growth.

We believe in seeing results fast. As an engineer with us, your work won't be lost in the bureaucratic shuffle. You'll witness the immediate impact of your contributions in real-time, influencing the evolution of our cutting-edge virtual fencing solution for livestock.

Join us, where ambition meets reality, and let's keep pushing the boundaries in the world of agri-tech!

About the Application
Please submit your application directly through this portal. In line with applicable data protection regulations and our data protection practices, we are unable to accept or process applications received by email. Applying through the portal also ensures your personal data is handled securely. We review applications on a rolling basis and look forward to hearing from you! 

If you have any questions about Nofence or regarding the application, please reach out to our Engineering Manager Kjetil Grimsæth at below email.

About Six Robotics
At Six Robotics, we build intelligent software that gives Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) the ability to collaborate, adapt on the fly, and execute missions that were previously impossible.

From our base in Oslo, our team of 90+ engineers, researchers, and defence specialists develops our autonomy and swarm platform, used by both government and industry. Working closely with the Norwegian Defence Research Establishment (FFI) and end users, we move quickly from ideas to field deployment, solving problems where software meets the real world.

The challenges we work on don’t come with existing playbooks. They demand deep technical thinking, close collaboration across disciplines, and the ability to learn quickly as both the technology and the company evolve.

At Six Robotics, every person executes with precision, adapts to changing conditions, and strengthens the team. If you’re excited about building systems that matter and growing alongside talented people that push boundaries every day, you’ll find no better place to deliver real-world impact.

About The Role
At Six Robotics, our product department is built around a clear flow: needs emerge from our customers, are shaped into product features, and are then translated into engineering-ready functionality. As we scale, we are strengthening our Product Team to own this flow end-to-end. This role will build and own the bridge between these domains, ensuring that what we ship is not driven by ad-hoc requests, but by validated needs from the field, strong technical context, and disciplined product decisions.

As a Product Manager at Six Robotics, you will turn complex project needs, field feedback, and long-term strategy into a coherent, executable product direction. This is a hands-on, operational product role at the center of engineering, projects, and real-world UAV operations.

You will help define where our software product, Valkyrie, is going. Defining what gets built, and why, without abstracting away the reality and context the engineering teams need to succeed and understand.

This role is critical in bringing stability, clarity, and long-term focus to how Valkyrie evolves, while still adapting to real-world demands from customers, field operations, and live deployments.

You will work closely with the other Product Managers and report to the Chief of Product, bringing clarity to our Engineering Team Leads, release and project management, acting as the bridge that ensures we build the right capabilities, at the right time, for the right reasons.

What You Will Do
• 
Translate project and customer requirements into actionable product features: prioritize, scope, and refine features so engineering can execute with clarity and confidence.

• 
Shape the product roadmap alongside the Head of Product: contribute to the vision, break it down into a detailed plan, and ensure it drives meaningful, deliverable work.

• 
Bring clarity to engineering to ensure we build the right features: minimize product debt, reduce ad-hoc feature work, and safeguard long-term product quality.

• 
Own operational product execution: track progress, manage priorities, and follow up on releases to keep product development structured and predictable.

• 
Maintain product clarity and coherence: oversee trade-offs, dependencies, and release content to ensure each feature delivers real value internally before reaching engineering.

• 
Validate and refine assumptions in the field: work and test the features with our field teams, to understand real-world performance and feed insights back into product decisions.

What we are looking for
We are looking for someone with exceptional structure and decision-making skills. We believe this person can confidently say no when needed, set direction, and still listen deeply to both the team and the customer. You thrive in ambiguity, bringing discipline and method where things feel uncertain, and you take ownership not just of your own work, but across teams and interfaces. You are comfortable challenging customers constructively, asking why they want something, and translating that into what is actually feasible and valuable for engineering to build. At the same time, you are hands-on, willing to dive into the details when necessary, without ever losing sight of priorities or long-term outcomes.

We believe the right candidate brings
• 
Proven experience working on the development of mission-critical software products, with clear ownership from idea to delivery.

• 
Strong understanding of the full product lifecycle - from requirements and specification to delivery, validation, and iteration.

• 
Strong background in building software products, with the ability to collaborate with engineers while keeping problems concrete and solvable.

• 
Experience in structuring and governing product flow - balancing prioritization, planning, dependencies, and release coordination.

• 
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to translate complex customer needs into clear engineering context, without losing the bigger picture.

• 
A competitive drive and delivery mindset. You care about outcomes, not just process.

• 
Fluency in English (Norwegian not required).

Nice-to-haves:

• 
Experience with UAVs, autonomy systems, robotics, or defence-related technology.

• 
Exposure to hardware-software integrated products or field-deployed systems.

Why you should join
• 
Build at the edge of what’s possible: You’ll work on problems the industry hasn’t solved yet, alongside people who are pushing the boundaries of autonomy, AI, and robotics.

• 
Grow as fast as the company: We believe that chance favours those in motion. The role you’re hired into is just the starting point. As Six Robotics evolves, so will your scope, your responsibilities, and your opportunities.

• 
Work with exceptional people: Surround yourself with people who raise your own standards. You’ll join a team of ambitious engineers and operators who care deeply about the quality of their work. Expectations are high, but so is the willingness to help each other improve.

• 
Ship work that matters. The things you build don't stay in a demo environment. They get deployed, tested, and used where reliability and performance genuinely matter.

• 
Supported by great benefits. Alongside meaningful work, we offer competitive compensation, equity potential, strong pension and insurance plans, gadget budgets, modern equipment, panoramic offices, and the flexibility you need to do your best work.

Our Recruitment Process
We want hiring to be transparent and respectful of your time. We aim to move with momentum while making thoughtful hiring decisions - because every new team member matters.

Our process typically includes:

• 
Initial phone screening (30 min): A conversation about your background, motivation, and the role.

• 
First interview (45 min): Meet the hiring team, learn more about Six Robotics, and discuss your experience.

• 
Second interview (60–90 min): A technical discussion/Case interview, typically including a take-home assignment with a case presentation.

• 
Final interview (45 min): Meet members of our leadership team to align expectations and answer any remaining questions.

Reference checks are conducted before an offer is finalized. We review applications continuously, so don't leave us hanging. Send us your application today!

Our Commitment to Inclusion
At Six Robotics, we are committed to creating a workplace built on respect, integrity, and collaboration. We value different perspectives and experiences, and we believe that diversity within our team strengthens both our work and our culture. We encourage all qualified candidates to apply and help us build technology that makes a real impact.

Security Clearance Requirement
All employees at Six Robotics must be eligible for security clearance. Some roles might require a high level of clearance, depending on the nature of the work. If you are hired, we’ll guide you through any required authorization or clearance process as part of your onboarding. Previous authorization or clearance is not required, but all candidates must be eligible to obtain the necessary approvals if required for their role.

jobs.occupation: PhD Position in Long-term Climate Governance
jobs.description:
PhD Position in Long-term Climate Governance
Oslo Business School at Oslo Metropolitan University (OsloMet) invites applications for a temporary position as PhD scholar in long-term climate governance. The position is connected to the ERC-funded research project CAMELOT – Capacities for More Effective Long-term Climate Governance and is expected to start in April 2027.

The position is three years full-time but can be extended to four years if teaching assignments are included. The PhD Research Fellow will be based in the academic unit Public Administration and Governance at Oslo Business School and will be enrolled in OsloMet's PhD programme in Social Sciences, specialization Business Administration, Innovation and Governance (BIG).

The successful candidate is expected to complete the doctoral degree during the period of employment.
About CAMELOT
Many of today's most consequential governance challenges, including climate change and Earth system risks, unfold over decades, centuries, or longer. Yet political institutions and decision-making processes often struggle to engage effectively with such long-term futures.

CAMELOT investigates the capacities that enable individuals, groups, and institutions to think about and govern for the long term. The project develops new theory on long-term governance capacities and studies whether and how such capacities can be strengthened through experimental and participatory research. It brings together insights from political science, public administration, environmental governance, sustainability science, futures studies, psychology, and related fields.

CAMELOT is a five-year research project funded by a European Research Council (ERC) Consolidator Grant and led by Associate professor Manjana Milkoreit at OsloMet.

CAMELOT project website
About the PhD project
The PhD scholar will develop an independent research project that contributes to CAMELOT's overarching objective of understanding and strengthening capacities for long-term climate governance.

The project should be theoretically informed and empirically grounded and involve original empirical research designed and conducted by the PhD candidate. The research may build on, extend, or enable comparisons with research undertaken elsewhere in CAMELOT, but should not depend on data collection undertaken in other parts of the project.

We welcome innovative proposals addressing questions related to long-term governance capacities. Possible research directions include, but are not limited to:

• investigating how narratives and stories about long-term climate futures influence imagination, understanding, attitudes, decision-making, or other capacities relevant to long-term governance
• examining how engagement with long-term climate futures differs across climate risks, Earth system tipping elements, audiences, social groups, professional communities, or political and cultural contexts
• studying how scenarios, foresight, simulations, serious games, or other futures-oriented interventions affect capacities for anticipatory and long-term governance
• developing and evaluating educational or professional interventions designed to strengthen capacities for engaging with long-term climate futures
• investigating whether and under what conditions changes in long-term governance capacities translate into changes in reasoning, decision-making, or action
Applicants are encouraged to propose original research questions and approaches that extend beyond these examples while demonstrating a clear connection to CAMELOT's overarching research agenda.

A range of methodological approaches may be appropriate, including quantitative, qualitative, experimental, and mixed-methods research. The proposed research must be feasible within the period of employment.

The candidate will conduct their own research while working closely with the CAMELOT team. They will benefit from interaction with CAMELOT's theoretical, experimental, and participatory research and may develop complementary or comparative studies building on concepts, methods, interventions, or findings developed within the project.
Qualification requirements
We are looking for candidates who meet the following requirements:

• master's degree of 120 ECTS or equivalent in political science, public administration, environmental governance, sustainability science, sociology, psychology, futures studies, science and technology studies, human geography, or another field relevant to the position
• grade of B or better on both the master's thesis and the master's degree overall, or an equivalent academic record
• demonstrate knowledge of research methods relevant to the proposed PhD project
• strong analytical and academic writing skills
• excellent written and spoken English
Candidates who are close to completing their master's degree may apply, provided that the degree is completed before the start of the position.

It will be an advantage

It will be considered an advantage to have knowledge of or previous research experience related to one or more of the following areas: climate or environmental governance; public policy; long-term or anticipatory governance; futures and foresight; environmental or political psychology; narratives and communication; Earth system risks and tipping points; or experimental and intervention-based social science.

Experience with empirical data collection and analysis, participation in research projects, academic publishing, or interdisciplinary research will also be considered an advantage.

General criteria for employment as a Research Fellow are stipulated in the Regulations relating to the Universities and University Colleges Act. 

Admission to the doctoral program is a prerequisite. Admission to the doctoral program is based on a comprehensive assessment of the application, including the relevance and quality of the project description. A finalized project plan for the employment period is required completed and acknowledged within 3 months from the date of employment.

See information about admission criteria to the PhD-programme.
